contexts.text: His Human essence is called a star out of Jacob, and a sceptre out of Israel ().
See Rod, Staff. AC 7026. AR 485:3. AE 431:2.

As a rod represented the power of truth, that is, the power of good through truth, kings had sceptres, and the sceptres were formed like short rods; for kings represented the Lord as to truth, (and) the sceptre = the power they have, not through dignity, but through the truth which must command, and no other truth than that which is from good; thus, principally. Divine truth; and, with Christians, the Lord from whom is all Divine truth.

The sceptre shall not he removed from Judah () = that the Power shall not recede from the Celestial Kingdom... A sceptre = Power, in fact, the Power of truth from good: for a sceptre is an ensign of royal Power; and by the royalty is signified truth. ( = that the Power shall not recede from the good of celestial love. AE 433:4.)
For tribe, and sceptre, in the Hebrew, are one word; and sceptre = kingdom: and the Lord's Kingdom is Heaven and the Church.
A king (when being crowned) held a sceptre in his right hand... For a sceptre, which is a rod, = the power of truth from good. References.
Thou shalt break the nations with an iron sceptre () = to chastise and master the evils in the natural man: a sceptre, here. = the like as a rod.
A sceptre of rectitude is the sceptre of Thy kingdom () = ... the Divine truth which has power and the kingdom.
There is in her no rod of strength, a sceptre of those who dominate () = the desolation of Divine truth as to power and as to dominion.
The sceptre of strength out of Zion () = the Divine truth which has omnipotence...
